items.title: Nemotron 3.5 Super VL Hugging Face: Checkpoints, Licence and How to Run
items.content:
The Nemotron 3.5 Super VL Hugging Face release gives you everything: open weights in BF16 and NVFP4, an OpenMDW-1.1 licence that allows commercial use, and recipes for vLLM, SGLang and Transformers. Nvidia also released training data and recipes. My video below covers the model. Here’s what’s on Hugging Face and how to run it.

Key takeaways

- Checkpoints: BF16 (full precision) and NVFP4 (optimised).

- Licence: OpenMDW-1.1 — commercial use allowed.

- Hardware for BF16: 4× H100 or 2× GB200.

- Community GGUF builds (e.g. Unsloth) for llama.cpp-based tools.

## What’s on Hugging Face

Repository
What it is

Optimised 4-bit weights for Nvidia hardware

Open datasets for agentic tool use, long context, vision-language and more

## Hardware requirements

The model card lists 4× H100 or 2× GB200 GPUs on Linux (Hopper or Blackwell) for the BF16 release. The NVFP4 version is designed for more efficient deployment, including on Nvidia’s DGX Spark desktop machine. For consumer setups, use the GGUF builds in LM Studio or Ollama (70GB+).

## How to run it with vLLM

The model card’s vLLM recipe serves it with tensor parallelism across four GPUs, multi-token-prediction speculative decoding, and the served name `nemotron-3.5-super-vl` on port 8000, using the vLLM OpenAI image (nightly or v0.32.0). Tool calling uses the `qwen3_coder` parser. SGLang (v0.5.20) is supported on two GB200s, and Transformers works through the image-text-to-text pipeline with `trust_remote_code`.

## Reasoning and video settings

- Reasoning modes: off, medium or on, set with `enable_thinking` and medium effort.

- Reasoning and the answer share the token budget.

- Video: up to 256 frames at 2 FPS (1 FPS and up to 128 frames suggested for 1080p).

- Inputs: text, JPEG/PNG images, document pages and MP4 video up to 2 minutes.

## The licence

Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is released under OpenMDW-1.1, and the model card says it’s ready for commercial or non-commercial use. As always, read the licence yourself before building a product on it.

## Should you self-host it?

Self-hosting makes sense for companies that need privacy, control or fine-tuning — Nvidia released the recipes to make that possible. For everyone else, OpenRouter’s free and cheap paid versions are far simpler.

Let me be clear: this is not a frontier model. It’s not going to replace Claude Opus 5.5 for your hardest work. What it is: a free, open, fast model that can read screenshots, PDFs and charts and then act on them — which is exactly the job a lot of agent work starts with.

## Fine-tuning Nemotron 3.5 Super VL

Because Nvidia released training recipes and datasets, you can fine-tune the model on your own data — your documents, your formats, your way of working. That’s most useful for companies with a specific, repeated visual task, like reading a particular kind of invoice or form. Fine-tuning a 120B model needs serious GPUs, so most teams will use cloud GPU providers rather than their own hardware.

## BF16 vs NVFP4

BF16 is the full-precision release: the best quality, but it needs the most memory. NVFP4 is a 4-bit format designed for Nvidia’s newer GPUs, cutting memory needs dramatically with little quality loss, which is what makes running it on smaller systems like DGX Spark possible. If you’re deploying on Nvidia Blackwell hardware, NVFP4 is usually the practical choice.

## Hosted alternatives

If self-hosting isn’t worth it for you, the same model is available through OpenRouter, Nvidia NIM, ModelScope and other hosts, and Together AI added it at launch. That gives you the open model without managing GPUs.

## Final thoughts

A last practical note: model cards are updated as recipes and benchmarks improve, so check the Hugging Face page for the latest serving instructions before you deploy. Nvidia’s recipes are tuned for its own hardware, and the community often publishes faster or smaller variants within days of a release — worth watching if you want to run it on less hardware.

If you just want to use the model rather than host it, skip all of this and use OpenRouter’s free or paid version, or try it free in OpenCode.

Open weights, open data and clear recipes make this one of the easiest big models to build on.

## How I’d test it this week

If you’re evaluating self-hosting, start by testing the hosted version on your real tasks. Only if it’s good enough — and you have a privacy, cost or customisation reason — is it worth renting GPUs to host it yourself.

When you do, start with the NVFP4 checkpoint on Blackwell hardware, follow the model card’s vLLM recipe, and benchmark throughput on your own prompts before committing.

## Common questions

Can I download it for free? Yes — the weights are free on Hugging Face. Can I use it commercially? The OpenMDW-1.1 licence allows commercial use, but read it yourself first. Do I need Nvidia GPUs? The official recipes target Nvidia Hopper and Blackwell GPUs; community GGUF builds run in llama.cpp-based tools like LM Studio and Ollama on other hardware. Is there a smaller version? Not of Super VL itself, but Nvidia’s Bolt 74B-A9B fits in 24GB of memory.

## The bottom line on Nemotron 3.5 Super VL Hugging Face

The Nemotron 3.5 Super VL Hugging Face release is unusually open: weights, data and recipes. If you have the GPUs, it’s a strong model to host yourself; if not, use the hosted versions.
